full_judgment:
to show cause as to why the impugned Judgment and decree dated 17.2.1990 passed by the learned District Judge, Cox's bazar, in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 9 of 1987 affirming the judgment and decree dated 24.12.1986 passed by the Learned Munsif, Chakaria, Cox's bazar in 

 Miscellaneous Case No. 174 of 1983 should not be set aside. 

 2. Facts leading to the issuance of this Rule are that the Opposite Party Hasan Ali instituted the other Suit No. 17 of 1977 in the Court of the Munsif, Chakaria, Cox's bazar praying for a decree for permanent injunction in respect of the suit property, described in the schedule to the plaint and the suit was decreed exparte on 4.4.1978. decree signed on 8.4.1978. As soon as the Plaintiff came to know about the exparte decree, filed an application on 17.6.1981 under Order IX Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure praying for restoration of the suit by setting aside the exparte decree on the grounds stated therein and it was registered as Miscellaneous Case NO. 174 of 1983 which, after hearing, was dismissed on 24.12.1986 vide Judgment and Order No. 52, passed by the Learned Munsif Chakaria, Cox's bazar and against the said judgment and order of dismissal the petitioner has preferred the Miscellaneous Appeal NO. 9 of 1987 and by his judgment and order dated 17.2.1990, the learned District Judge, Cox's bazar has also been pleased to dismiss the Appeal on contest upholding the judgment and order dated 24.12.1986 passed by the learned Munsif Being aggrieved by the said judgment and order, the Petitioner-Appellant has preferred this application under Section 115(1) of the Court of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained the instant Rule on the grounds that the learned Appellate Court has erred in law in not holding that the service return of the Process Server was not accompanied by any Affidavit or even verification or a declaration as was required by law and examination of the Process Server was essential and that the learned Appellate Court has committed an error in his decision occasioning failure of justice in not holding that inspite of provisions of Rule I 9A of Order V of the Code of Civil Procedure-, examination of the Process Server in the instant case was mandatory, as the Process Server has simply submitted his report about the service of summons without any verification or declaration and the learned Court has also erred in law in not holding that the summons has not been served upon the Defendant. 

 3. Mr. J.B.M. Hasan, the learned Advocate appearing for the Petitioner, by placing his reliance upon the case of Abdul Wahab Gazi Vs. Sheikh Haider Ali and others. reported in 1 BLC(AD) 41 submitted that the learned trial Court without finding that the summons was duly served upon the Defendants passed the exparte decree and that the onus to prove that the summons was duly served upon the Defendants was on the Plaintiff and the onus was not discharged when the Process Server has simply submitted his report about the. service of summons by affixing without any verification or declaration, and not examined whereas, his examination is mandatory under Order V Rule 17, 19 and 19A of the Code of Civil Procedure, when the service is by hanging. The learned Appellate Court has erred in law in not looking into the matter in Appeal which has occasioned failure of justice. 

 4. Mr. Rabi Shankar Chakraborty. the learned Advocate, appearing for the: opposite Party, has on the other hand, relied upon the case of Md. Insan Ali Vs Mir Abdus Salam, reported in 40 DI.,11(AD) 193, upon which the learned Appellate Court has also placed his reliance and held that the onus has shifted upon the Defendant to prove that the summons was not duly served, as claimed by the Plaintiffs and it was incumbent upon all the Defendants to depose on oath that summons were not served upon them by the Process Server. Relying upon the principle enunciated in this case, the Learned Advocate supported the decision of the Learned Appellate Court praying for discharge of the Rule. 

 9. In the instant case, the learned Appellate Court found that the Plaintiff-Opposite Party has clearly discharged his onus as the Process Server submitted his report along with a declaration that he served the summons by hanging it on the gate of the Defendants, when the later refused to accept it and thereafter, the plaintiff appeared in the Court and deposed on oath that the summons has duly been served and the Defendants could not prove that they were prevented by sufficient causes from appearing in the suit on the date fixed for hearing and they have also failed to prove suppression of summons as alleged. 

 10. In the case of Md. Insan Ali Vs. Mir Abdus Salam, reported in 40 DLR (AD) 193 

 learned Munsif nowhere recorded his satisfaction that the summons has been served upon the Defendants and the service was satisfactory. Without recording his Satisfaction about service, he has disposed of the suit exparte and as such, the instant suit is distinguishable from the case reported in 40 DLR (AD) 193 and the case law enunciated in the reported case, supports the 

 above is categorical that ".... The declaration made and subscribed by the serving officer shall he received as evidence of the facts as to the service or attempted to service of summons' meaning that the learned Judge concerned, in such a case must take into cognizance the service of summons and admit the service or attempted to service into evidence on his expressed satisfaction and otherwise it means that he shall record his satisfaction in his exparte decree about the service of summons. Thus before proceeding for exparte disposal a judge needs to record that the summons have been served upon the Defendants to his satisfaction and only after that he can proceed with the suit for exparte disposal and this pre-condition of satisfaction 

 regarding service and admitting it into evidence is, of course, lacking in the instant suit. If considered from the factual aspects of this case it is also not believable that a man would sit idle even knowing that he has been restrained by a court by injunction from entering into a land with which he is involved in a dispute. 

 13. In the case Abdul Wahab Gazi Vs. Sheikh Haider Ali, reported in 1 BLC (AD) 41 their lordships have considered the provisions of Rule 17, 19 and 19A of the Order V of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

 The impugned Judgment and decree, dated 17.2.1990 passed by the learned District Judge, Cox's bazar, in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 9 of 1987 dismissing the Appeal and affirming the judgment and decree dated 24.12.1986 passed by the Learned Munsif: Chakaria, C'ox's bazar in Miscellaneous Case No. 174 of 1983 is hereby set aside.
